77569.subject: Commerce
77569.question_text:
(a) Differentiate between a merger and an acquisition

(b) Explain five ways commerce is important in the life of a nation
77569.explanation:
(a) Merger is the coming together or amalgamation of two or more firms to form one new company. By merging, the firm
will grow in size and maintain large scale production while an acquisition oocur when one company buys another
company and fold it into its operations. Sometimes the purchase is friendly and sometimes it is hostile, depending on
whether the company being acquired believes it is better off as an operating unit of a larger venture.

(b) - Employment opportunities: It offers employment opportunites to a large number of people such as a traders, bankers,
insurance brokers, etc.
- Raising of capital: It facitatess the raising of capital for individual needs and investment through the services of banks
and other financial institutions
- Exchange of Goods and services: It facilitates the exchange of goods and services through transportation and
telecommunication services
- Creation of Public Awareness: It makes the public awaren of the availability of goods and services through
advertising
- Creation of wealth for Nations: Commerce helps to create wealth for nations, as duties are charged on goods and
services either exported or imported.

77570.subject: Commerce
77570.question_text:
(i) Differentiate between the following pairs of terms:
- Interest and profit 

(ii) Differentiate between the following pairs of terms:
- Share and debenture

(iii) Differentiate between the following pairs of terms:
Ordinary share and preference share

(iv) Differentiate between the following pairs of terms:
- Cummulative preference share and participating preference share

(v) Differentiate between the following pairs of terms:
- Cum div and ex div
77570.explanation:
(i) Interest is the reward for capital as a factor of production . Interest is income that lenders (usually banks) make a loans
while profit is the reward for an entreprenuer as a factor of production, profit is the net result of a company's income.

(ii) Shares (Equity securities): An individual portion of the company's capital or a unit of capital measured by a sum of
money. When shares are fully paid, they can be converted into stock
Debenture: A document setting out the terms of loan to a company i.e. it is a certificate of indebtedness and bearing a
fixed rate of interest.

(iii) Ordinary shares: Also known as "Equity". These are shares whose holders received dividend only after the preference
shareholders have received dividend. They are regarded as risk bearer and not entitled to a fixed rate of interest.
Preference shares: These are share whose holders receive dividends at specific rates and ahead of ordinary dows
shareholders and also holders are not entitled to partake in the surplus in liquidation unless the Articles of Association
stipulate otherwise

(iv) Cumulative preference shares: These are preference shares in which unpaid arrears (i.e. arrears of previous years) of
dividends are accumulated yearly and must be fully paid from the profits of the subsequent years before ordinary
dividends are paid. They are carried forward.
Participating preference shares: These are shares which after receiving their nominal dividend also have the rightto
participate in the excess dividend after ordinary shares have been paid.

(v) CUM-DIV: Means the shareholder (buyer) will be entitled to the next dividend.
EX-DIV: Means the shareholder (buyer) will not be entitled to the next dividend

77571.subject: Commerce
77571.question_text:
(a) State four function of money

(bi) Explain how the following operators function on a stock exchange
- Bull

(bii) Explain how the following operators function on a stock exchange
- Jobber

(biii) Explain how the following operators function on a stock exchange
- Broker

(iv) Explain how the following operators function on a stock exchange
- Stag
77571.explanation:
(a) - As a medium of exchange
- As a store of value
- As a unit of account
- As a standard for deferred payment

(bi) Bull: A speculator who buys securities with the intention of reselling them at a high price. If the price falls, he loses and
has the option to carry forward the transaction to the next settlement by paying a charge termed "Contango".

(bii) Jobbers: Jobbers are professional speculators who perform important functions as member of the stock exchange.
Jobbers are independent dealer in securities and transact them in his own. They deal only with members of stock
exchanges like broker of other jobber and do not interact with a non-member.

(biii) Brokers are public agent who acts as an intermediary between the public and jobbers working at the stock exchange.
They link the jobbers and the public.

(iv) Stags: This is a speculator that applies for new stocks and shares in large quantity with the hope that the prices of
securities will rise before selling them.

77573.subject: Commerce
77573.question_text:
(a) What is entreport trade?

(bi) Differentiate between a bill of lading and a consignment note

(bii) Explain the use of bill of sight in foreign trade

(c) State five reasons for the criticism against advertising
77573.explanation:
(a) Entreport trade is a trade in which goods shipped to one port are re-exported and shipped to another part. It is also the
re-exporting of goods imported from other nations.

(bi) A bill of lading is a contract of carriage of goods between an exporter and the shipping company while a consignment
note is a document made out by the sender of goods, signed by the consignee on delivery as proof of delivery.

(bii) - The document enables the goods to be landed and their inspection is authorised by the custom
- The document has a full description of the goods that will be provided later
- It is a document used in import trade
- It is a document submitted to the custom authorities if the full description of the imported goods cannot be provided.

(c) - It leads to Monopoly
- It can lead to unhealthy competition
- It interferes with the free choice of consumers
- Advertising encourages buyers to make unnecessary purchases
- Advertising appeals mainly to the irrational motives in people.

77574.question_text:
(ai) Madam Fana, the human resources manager of Baku limited, is due to start her annual leave. She wishes to assign one of
her assistants to perform her duties in her absence.
- Identify and explain the organizational principle on which Madam Fana has based her decision

(aii) Madam Fana, the human resources manager of Baku limited, is due to start her annual leave. She wishes to assign one
of her assistants to perform her duties in her absence.
- State four duties of Madam Fana in Baku limited

(bi) Explain the following management functions:

(bii) Explain the following management functions:

- Organizing

(biii) Explain the following management functions:
- Directing

(iv) Explain the following management functions:
- Controlling
77574.explanation:
(ai) The organizational principle identified here is the Principle of Delegation of Authority.
Delagation of authority is the transfer of authority from the superior to the subordinate to carry out the assignment
while the superior will consider himself/herself accountable for the delegated job.

(aii) - To recruit new staff, interviewing and oversee the recruiting/hiring process
- Determining suitable salaries and remuneration
- Providing the necessary support systems for payroll requirements
- Managing company staff, including cordinating and supporting the recruitment process.
- Developing adequate induction and training

(bi) This is the first and most important functions of Management. It allows the manager to choose the appropriate goals and
actions to pursue in order to determine the organizational objectives.

(bii) This is the process of establishing worker relationship which allows the workers to work together to achieve their
organizational goals.

(biii) This involves getting people to carry out the decisions quickly, efficiently and with minimum fuss

(iv) Controlling is a key management function that involves monitoring and evaluating the performance of an organization to
ensure that it is meeting its goals and objectives. The controlling process includes setting performance standards,
measuring actual performance, comparing it with the established standards, and taking corrective actions if necessary.
